items.title: Tim Ries interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 19, 2022
items.q: he started scheduling improvisation lessons, and he played the organ and piano and trumpet and trombone, and he was a very musical guy named Mike Lorenz. He was great. And that was it. It was kind of like opening the door to like now, I get the theoretical idea of it

ctx.x: Well I was just thinking that now, because I’m wondering if you learned how to improvise before you had any theoretical basis for what you were doing?

I did. And just I think to capture mostly that feeling of seeing him, because I had an older brother who died and he was the oldest and I was the youngest. So I often wonder if, me having three children, I can’t imagine that happening. So I wonder also if that was his going into that other world or something. But I just — he was very different at the piano than — on the trumpet he was like beautiful sound, amazing tone. In fact I remember as a little kid being on one of his gigs, and it was a dance gig. And he…
now theoretically what is this chord, how do you do that, and then to dissect the chord and then I started composing.
